brief: Goldman Sachs' Financial Conditions Index has tightened about 100bp this year, all since early September, with over 40bp last week alone, driven by the year's rate rise plus the recent equity decline and dollar appreciation. If the tightening persists it adds a 0.5pp drag to both 2026Q4 and 2027 Q4/Q4 GDP growth on top of GS's 2027 forecast of 2.4% growth, a bit more than its October FOMC-level estimate implied. GS calls the move short-lived: if its own strategists' forecasts for equities and long rates prove right, more than half the tightening reverses next year with no extra drag. On the Fed, GS still expects a second 25bp December hike (near certainty) and a third hike in March, because the tightening matches what FOMC officials already expect from 75-100bp of total hikes, part of it stems from hike expectations that could unwind on their own, and today's high inflation and above-potential growth make the FOMC less likely to blink as in 2016 or 2018. Risk: a risk-sentiment or AI-spending-driven selloff could still displace 2027 hikes, trim the December dot plot, or ease hike need by cooling the core PCE pressure AI demand is adding.
